newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mexico pledges greater safety for foreign executives.
newsitem.headline: Mexico pledges greater safety for foreign executives.

text.p: Mexico has increased its police budget and training to prevent kidnappings and other crimes against foreign executives, Mexican Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz told Japanese business officials on Wednesday.
"This year we have a budget for public safety which is 10 times larger than what we spent last year," Ortiz said.

Japanese firms have expressed fears about security in Mexico after a California-based executive from an affiliate of Japan's Sanyo Corp was kidnapped last August by armed men near the Mexico-U.S. border town of Tijuana.
The executive was released after the firm paid a ransom, but the incident prompted security concerns, which Tokyo executives raised with Ortiz on Wednesday.

"This is a problem that we cannot solve overnight, but we will be hiring professional consultants and systems, and computers in order to build a modern police force," Ortiz told a seminar sponsored by the Nihon Keizai Shimbun, a Japanese business daily newspaper.
Mexico's Secretary of Commerce Herminio Blanco, speaking at the symposium, called for more investment in Mexico by Japan's small and medium-sized firms.
"What we need right now is...the second generation of migration of companies to Mexico -- small and medium-sized corporations," Blanco said. "Most large Japanese companies are already in Mexico."
Ortiz, Blanco and other senior Mexican officials are accompanying Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo on a four-day state visit to Japan, which will end on Friday.
On Wednesday, Zedillo addressed the Japanese parliament and held talks with Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.
